title: Production Database Recovery Execution

preflight.decision: STOP before starting production PostgreSQL or performing cutover

forensic_preservation.production_volume: football-agent_pgdata; untouched and still mounted by stopped football-postgres container

cold_tar.method: read-only mount of the stopped production volume, no-network one-shot container, tar archive

fresh_dump_from_cold_clone.method: restore cold tar to new football-task063-forensic-clone Docker volume; start isolated no-network clone; run pg_dump -Fc; pg_restore -l readable
fresh_dump_from_cold_clone.note: A direct live production pg_dump remains required after administrator-level writer freeze and before cutover.

expected_from_TASK_062.known_minimum_gap: 95 fixtures, 7 predictions, 1 bookmaker; later writes UNKNOWN

required_before_resuming: Use an Administrator Windows context to enumerate the full FootballAgent Scheduler topology and verify or temporarily freeze every PostgreSQL-writing task without permanent definition changes.
Confirm no writer/Alembic processes and no stale locks immediately before starting production PostgreSQL.
After the writer freeze is proven, take a direct fresh pg_dump of the live damaged production database; keep the cold tar and clone dump as extra forensic copies.
Only then follow the exact TASK-062 staging restore, 0020 to 0021 upgrade, exact verification, and data-preserving cutover/rollback procedure.

requested_result_fields.ALEMBIC_REVISION: damaged database 0021 ledger only; recovered production not yet available
requested_result_fields.FORENSIC_DAMAGED_BACKUP: cold pgdata tar plus custom pg_dump from isolated cold clone; direct live dump pending

stop_reason: The current Windows token cannot read canonical scheduled tasks. Production PostgreSQL is stopped, and restarting it before proving all writers frozen could allow an unseen writer to run during cutover.
